rv.q: He is also trapped, unfortunately, inside an ambitious but awkward production whose elements battle one another more often than not.
There are fine ideas within Mary Shelley'S FRANKENSTEIN, but stronger dramaturgy and deeper execution are required to bring them to life.
The overall show is less than the sum of its parts.
Spectacular by Off-Broadway standards, Mary Shelley's Frankenstein never gels into an arresting theater piece.

Fairchild delivers a heroic performance, exposing in arresting movement and dance – sometimes achingly convulsive, sometimes soaring – the yearning soul inside the hideous exterior of Frankenstein's human – and yet non-human – contraption.
Though the concept has potential, not all the pieces gel and as a whole, the piece seems disjointed, thanks to director Donald T. Sanders.
Too bad this play is not [a masterpiece].
The story and this production is as lost as that Monster flailing around in the woods.
